snapshot.stmt: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) be completed into a multi-district theorem that projects the full source-labelled compatibility fiber onto the exact product-constrained faces needed for \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\), so that every failed arm-order certificate yields two original-alphabet SCM families with opposite ranking, or does the smallest binary two-hedge thicket contain a recursive failure whose target score is already constant on the global fiber?

defs.def:cross-menu-preservation-handle: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) starts from the exact feasible face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and tracks both its affine hull and forced-zero coordinates through ancestor restriction, fixing, district splitting, and marginalization in \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).

snapshot.stmt:
The minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are computable for every finite instance by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and solving the finite linear feasibility problems that define \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
 =\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem reduces to
\[
 \min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two.
The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]
defs.def:target-arm-rows: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
 <\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta).
\]
In particular, a target structural-causal bandit may safely prune \(\rho\) in favor of \(\sigma\) exactly when the first strict minimum condition holds.

For every district \(D\), the global projection satisfies
\[
 \{q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}
 \subseteq \mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
A local point, or a pair of local points, lifts to globally compatible SCM families exactly when it belongs, or they both belong, to the left-hand projection.  Equality with \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) follows under the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem, but is not implied in a multi-district problem.  Hence a local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) face-failure trace alone is not a global paired-model certificate; the exact multi-district certificate is instead furnished by distinct optimizers of the displayed global polynomial programs.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.

defs.def:incidence-row: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]
defs.def:stacked-menu-system: For every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\). Only then retain, for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), the row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\). Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the retained rows as \(A_D\), and stack one and the retained kernel cells as \(m_D\). Failed extraction creates no row.

defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced target and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). A target row \(b_D\) is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) if and only if \[b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}.\] If \(b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\), its value is \(\lambda^\top m_D\). If the membership fails, two SCM families on \(\mathcal X\) agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:dctftr-grammar:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).
defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) canonically and retain a context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds and a checked proof gives \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\); the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed extraction and changed-district rejection without creating a row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district relaxation and is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless the one-district fiber-projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization extraction succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

snapshot.stmt: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

defs.def:allowed-rational-functional: \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is the typed expression-and-certificate algebra generated from menu cells by finite sums, differences, products, marginalization sums, and quotients carrying a proof that the divisor is nonzero on the relevant compatibility fiber.
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) canonically and retain a context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds and a checked proof gives \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\); the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed extraction and changed-district rejection without creating a row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district relaxation and is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless the one-district fiber-projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization extraction succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\), and the one-domain problem-instance class has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\) obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\). On either embedded class, every successful identifying functional returned by DCTFTR agrees semantically with the target query, and every successful functional returned by the published calculus agrees with that same query; no syntactic or transition-by-transition output equivalence is asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), CTFTR cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is not a single-specification CTFIDU+ instance.

defs.def:binary-check: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.\] Consequently, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every compatible SCM if and only if the displayed dual has a certificate with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), a primal minimizer induces an original-alphabet compatible SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\), primal minimizers and maximizers induce two original-alphabet compatible SCMs with opposite arm rankings.

defs.def:dual-dominance-certificate: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces are obtained from the feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of one closed interval, allowing zero, one, or two sign boundaries; each boundary returns both a dual menu-weight certificate on the pruning side and an original-alphabet SCM attaining equality.

For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).

Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\). If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0\), removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); an arm whose common evidence is certified zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.

Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced arm targets and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). In particular, every point of the boundary face, not only its relative interior, is induced by a compatible SCM family on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced target and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). A target row \(b_D\) is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) if and only if \[b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}.\] If \(b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\), its value is \(\lambda^\top m_D\). If the membership fails, two SCM families on \(\mathcal X\) agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.

defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.\] Consequently, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every compatible SCM if and only if the displayed dual has a certificate with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), a primal minimizer induces an original-alphabet compatible SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\), primal minimizers and maximizers induce two original-alphabet compatible SCMs with opposite arm rankings.

defs.def:dual-dominance-certificate: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces are obtained from the feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of one closed interval, allowing zero, one, or two sign boundaries; each boundary returns both a dual menu-weight certificate on the pruning side and an original-alphabet SCM attaining equality.

For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).

defs.def:binary-check: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\). If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0\), removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); an arm whose common evidence is certified zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.

The minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are computable for every finite instance by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and solving the finite linear feasibility problems that define \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
 =\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem reduces to
\[
 \min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two.
The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]
defs.def:target-arm-rows: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
 <\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta).
\]
In particular, a target structural-causal bandit may safely prune \(\rho\) in favor of \(\sigma\) exactly when the first strict minimum condition holds.

For every district \(D\), the global projection satisfies
\[
 \{q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}
 \subseteq \mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
A local point, or a pair of local points, lifts to globally compatible SCM families exactly when it belongs, or they both belong, to the left-hand projection.  Equality with \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) follows under the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem, but is not implied in a multi-district problem.  Hence a local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) face-failure trace alone is not a global paired-model certificate; the exact multi-district certificate is instead furnished by distinct optimizers of the displayed global polynomial programs.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), retain a separate graph-compatible canonical parameter \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its simplex and one-hot coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the finite recursive canonical cell polynomial and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be its induced joint response-profile law on \(D\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:incidence-row: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.
defs.def:target-arm-rows: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced arm targets and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). In particular, every point of the boundary face, not only its relative interior, is induced by a compatible SCM family on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[

\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[

\qquad

For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row

r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\). A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.

assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the union of variables visited by the reduced target and every retained menu factor has one district \(D\), and \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). A target row \(b_D\) is constant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) if and only if \[b_D\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}.\] If \(b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\), its value is \(\lambda^\top m_D\). If the membership fails, two SCM families on \(\mathcal X\) agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell.

defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. defs.def:dctftr-grammar:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).
defs.def:dctftr-recursion:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) and their complete cells canonically.  After a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), first retain every complete cell whose recursive indicator visits only \(D\) as the raw equality \(P_a^s(v)=r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}q_D^\star\).  Then retain a derived context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds with the same admissibility proof; the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed derived extraction, changed-district rejection, and cross-district raw cell without turning it into a district row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted raw and derived rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district row relaxation.  It is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless district saturation and the district-separated one-district projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization raw or derived row succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

snapshot.stmt: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\), and the one-domain problem-instance class has a proper typed embedding \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\hookrightarrow\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\) obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\). On either embedded class, every successful identifying functional returned by DCTFTR agrees semantically with the target query, and every successful functional returned by the published calculus agrees with that same query; no syntactic or transition-by-transition output equivalence is asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), CTFTR cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is not a single-specification CTFIDU+ instance.

defs.def:binary-check: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
