If no non-normalization raw or derived row succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.\] Consequently, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every compatible SCM if and only if the displayed dual has a certificate with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), a primal minimizer induces an original-alphabet compatible SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\). If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\), primal minimizers and maximizers induce two original-alphabet compatible SCMs with opposite arm rankings.

defs.def:dual-dominance-certificate: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\), \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\), and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces are obtained from the feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of one closed interval, allowing zero, one, or two sign boundaries; each boundary returns both a dual menu-weight certificate on the pruning side and an original-alphabet SCM attaining equality.

For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).

defs.def:binary-check: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

snapshot.stmt:
The minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are computable for every finite instance by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and solving the finite linear feasibility problems that define \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\).  In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular.  In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
 \operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
 =\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns.  For this instance the exact acquisition problem reduces to
\[
 \min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two.
The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:regime-block-acquisition: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]
defs.def:target-arm-rows: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\).  The set \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set of finite dimension, and canonical realization on the declared observed alphabets gives, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
 \bigl\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):
       \mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\bigr\}
 =
 \bigl\{(\Phi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
       \theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\bigr\}.
\]
Consequently, the extrema \(L_T(\mathcal P)\) and \(U_T(\mathcal P)\) are attained and are the sharp bounds for every target cell \(T\).  The bounds are strictly tighter than the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when \(L_T(\mathcal P)>0\) or \(U_T(\mathcal P)<1\), an exactly checkable property of the displayed program.  The cell is identified if and only if \(L_T(\mathcal P)=U_T(\mathcal P)\); if \(L_T(\mathcal P)<U_T(\mathcal P)\), minimizing and maximizing canonical parameters yield two SCM families on the original observed alphabets that agree on every cell of every complete supplied law and disagree on \(T\).

Let
\[
 e_-=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star),
 \qquad
 e_+=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star).
\]
If \(e_+ =0\), the evidence has probability zero throughout the compatibility fiber; if \(e_-=0<e_+\), its positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If \(e_->0\), the sharp range of the conditional arm value is
\[
 \left[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)},
 \quad
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \frac{\Phi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)}
      {\Phi_E^\star(\theta^\star)}
 \right],
\]
with both endpoints attained.  Under the same condition \(e_->0\), uniform strict ordering satisfies
\[
 \begin{array}{rcl}
 Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)>0,\\[3pt]
 Q_\rho^\star>Q_\sigma^\star\text{ in every compatible SCM}
 &\Longleftrightarrow&
 \displaystyle\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}
 \mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0,
 \end{array}
\]
and two original-alphabet compatible families with opposite strict rankings exist if and only if
\[
 \min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)<0
 <\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta).
\]
In particular, a target structural-causal bandit may safely prune \(\rho\) in favor of \(\sigma\) exactly when the first strict minimum condition holds.

For every district \(D\), the global projection satisfies
\[
 \{q_D^\star(\cdot;\theta^\star):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}
 \subseteq \mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
A local point, or a pair of local points, lifts to globally compatible SCM families exactly when it belongs, or they both belong, to the left-hand projection.  Equality with \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) follows under the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem, but is not implied in a multi-district problem.  Hence a local \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) face-failure trace alone is not a global paired-model certificate; the exact multi-district certificate is instead furnished by distinct optimizers of the displayed global polynomial programs.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), retain a separate graph-compatible canonical parameter \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its simplex and one-hot coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the finite recursive canonical cell polynomial and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be its induced joint response-profile law on \(D\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. Equality for the saturated fiber follows only under \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) by the one-district fiber-projection theorem. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside that theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-saturated-model-class:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), retain a separate graph-compatible canonical parameter \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its simplex and one-hot coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained. Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

For every district \(D\),

defs.def:district-saturated-model-class:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}

defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\). A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.

Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the saturated fiber. Without the additional hypotheses, the primal optimizers need not lift from the row face.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the row-augmented supplied menu at that boundary has nonempty \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\) and satisfies \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), the equality law is realized by a district-saturated SCM on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\). Without those hypotheses, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.

snapshot.stmt:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For a sparse nonsaturated graph or a cross-district-coupled menu, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is only an outer relaxation. If \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
which requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of all \(D'\ne D\). This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation is what makes the displayed multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

snapshot.stmt:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]

\]

\[

A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. snapshot.stmt:
Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the focal-district-saturated fiber. Under these additional hypotheses, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet compatible focal-district-saturated SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\), and \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\) yields two such SCM families with opposite strict rankings while preserving every other district's graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) remains sufficient for the active-slice hypothesis. Without the additional hypotheses, the primal optimizers need not lift from the row face.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:dual-dominance-certificate: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the supplied menu augmented by the boundary equality \(r_D^\dagger q=p\) has a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber and satisfies its \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\) predicate, the equality law is realized by an SCM saturated only at \(D\) on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\), with every district \(D'\ne D\) retaining its original graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) is a sufficient check for this active-slice condition. Without those hypotheses, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.

snapshot.stmt:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
and \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) itself entails a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber. This equality requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of every \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell is harmless for the fixed-baseline replacement exactly when its baseline-averaged focal row lies in \(R_D(m_D)\), because
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a baseline-free sufficient certificate for this equality. The baseline-averaged predicate is generally baseline-dependent and not directly checkable from menu cells alone; allowing a different baseline for each candidate \(q\) is not asserted. Outside focal-district saturation and baseline-averaged separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation makes the multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.

defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-saturated-model-class:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\). defs.def:exact-global-canonical-fiber:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the finite recursive canonical cell polynomial and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be its induced joint response-profile law on \(D\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).

\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]
defs.def:saturated-compatibility-fiber:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

assumptions.ass:district-closure: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).
assumptions.ass:district-factorization: In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.

defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:incidence-row: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]
defs.def:stacked-menu-system:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.
defs.def:target-arm-rows: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).
defs.def:typed-extraction-judgment: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

assumptions.ass:district-kernel-invariance: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).
assumptions.ass:recursive-compatibility: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions.ass:typed-menu-realizability: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  This predicate entails \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{span}\{q-q':q,q'\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}^{\perp}.
\]
For the single witnessing baseline \(\mathbf M^0\) in \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), every transport-admissible complete supplied cell is preserved under replacement of its focal law \(q_0\) by an arbitrary \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) because
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}(q-q_0)=0.
\]
Every boundary point of the row face is therefore induced on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) by a compatible SCM family saturated only at \(D\), while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) together with \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and hence also together with \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), is a convenient sufficient condition for \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  Without baseline-averaged separation or focal-district saturation, only the displayed broad inclusion is asserted.

defs.def:active-slice-separated-menu:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.
defs.def:baseline-averaged-active-slice-menu:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  For a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), let
\[
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
=\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}q_{D'}^{0,s}(\omega_{D'}),
\qquad
\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'},
\]
where \(q_{D'}^{0,s}\) is the response-profile law induced by \(M^{0,s}\).  For every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), define the baseline-averaged focal row
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}
=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu_{-D}^{0,s}(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}
\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
The baseline-averaged active-slice predicate \(\mathsf{BASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when there exists one \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
\bar\chi_{C_{a,v}}^{s,\mathbf M^0}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell.  The same witnessing baseline must be used for all cells and all feasible replacements of the focal law; a baseline depending on the replacement law is not permitted.
defs.def:compatibility-fiber: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]
defs.def:compatible-face:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
defs.def:district-response-profile: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).
defs.def:district-separated-menu: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).
defs.def:focal-district-saturated-model-class:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.
